localChanges: chore: update civ1-government, civ1-wonder and simple-ai-client

log: `Revolution` used to be applied by the client, which set the chosen government straight away. Now:

`lib/revolution.ts` owns the change. `revolution()` puts the player into Anarchy for as many turns as the new `AnarchyDuration` rules allow (the shortest answer wins; the default is 1-4, Rome on 640K a Day p18-19) and records the choice it owes as a `PendingEffect` targeting the `PlayerGovernment`, with the turn it falls due. `chooseGovernment()` discharges it. The handler is registered with the rules, so a game loaded mid-Anarchy can still finish its revolution.

`ChooseGovernment` (mandatory) is offered once the choice is due. `Revolution` is withdrawn while one is pending, which covers a zero-turn revolution (the Pyramids) where the government hasn't changed yet.
`Anarchy` is registered in the available governments, so a save taken during it can name the class. No `Availability` rule matches it, so it is never offered.
Adds the package's first tests, including a save/load round trip.

Copies civ1-wonder's build-on-push.yml: current Node and actions, pnpm with web-renderer's settings, a real prettier:check and npm test (the old workflow ran yarn on Node 18 and never ran tests; there were none). Removes yarn.lock and .yarnrc.yml, which nothing reads after the switch.
Both effects from Rome on 640K a Day p314-315, while the owner has the Pyramids and nobody has discovered Communism (the point `Player/research-complete` makes them obsolete):
an `AnarchyDuration` rule returning 0, so a revolution goes straight to choosing a government;
an `Availability` rule offering Communism, Democracy, Despotism, Monarchy and Republic whatever the owner's advances.
Needs civ1-government's `AnarchyDuration` and `lib/revolution`. Refs civ-clone/web-renderer#33 and civ-clone/web-renderer#30.

civ1-government, core-engine and civ1-city-happiness are imported by the rules but were undeclared (civ1-city-happiness only as a devDependency), resolving only through hoisting. core-tile-improvement and core-city-growth are imported by tests. civ1-government is github: to match web-renderer. Removes yarn.lock and .yarnrc.yml, as decided on #66 once a repo is on the pnpm workflow.

The AI set Monarchy directly, skipping `Revolution`. It now calls civ1-government's `revolution()` once it knows Monarchy (when not already in Monarchy, in Anarchy, or waiting on a revolution), and answers the `ChooseGovernment` mandatory action (Monarchy if available, otherwise the first available government). An unhandled mandatory item would otherwise hit `Can't process` and end the loop.
Takes a `PendingEffectRegistry` as a new last constructor argument, defaulting to the singleton.
SimpleAIClient.ts and Rules/City/* import both, but they were only devDependencies.
